newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: MOZAMBIQUE CAHORA BASSA DAM TO HAVE POWER RESTORED.
newsitem.headline: MOZAMBIQUE CAHORA BASSA DAM TO HAVE POWER RESTORED.

text.p: Power to one of Africa's largest hydro electric dams in Mozambique will be restored in April after a break of more than 10 years, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

Mozambique's mineral resources and energy minister, John Kachamila, told the Mozambique News Agency he expected power lines for the Cahora Bass hydro electric station, linking the dam to neighbouring South Africa, to be restored by the end of April.
Kachamila said the recently rehabilitated dam will save Mozambique about $10 million currently spent every year on importing electricity from South Africa.
The dam will provide almost 2,000 megawatts (MW) of hydro electric power through 1,400 km of power lines to the Apollo substation north of Johannesburg.

The dam and power station, restored at a cost of 575 million rand, will be operated by Mozambique's Hidroelectrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB) together with the Portuguese government and South Africa's Eskom Ltd company.
Electricity supply from Cahora Bassa to South Africa was interrupted in 1982 when about 1,800 pylons were sabotaged by Renamo rebels and South Africa's apartheid military forces during the civil war.
Just one percent of the dam is currently being used to supply electricity to the nearby towns of Tete and Songo.
The Cahora Bassa project will turn Mozambique from an importer of electricity to a net exporter boosting its war damaged economy which relies heavily on foreign aid.

Currently there is no direct power line from Cahora Bassa to the Mozambican capital Maputo, but under an agreement with Eskom the electricity that Maputo receives from South Africa will be treated as Cahora Bassa power.
Mozambique will be allowed to import up to 200 MW of electricity from South Africa which will be payable to the HCB. Eskom will only be paid rental for the line.
Kachamila said a new power supply line from Cahora Bassa to its western neighbour Zimbabwe will also be completed soon.
"This line will operate as an experiment until the third quarter of 1997 when the power will be supplied on commercial terms'', Kachamila said.
Power lines will later be extended to the southern Mozambican cities of Inhambane and Xai-Xai.
